hypothesis.text: Given a harness scaffolded by `npx metaharness <name>` with any host set that ends up registering an MCP server (today: every scaffold using the default claude-code host), when the generator additionally emits ADR-022's default-deny .harness/mcp-policy.json gated on the same registration signal mcp-scan.ts's own mcpEnabled check uses, then harness mcp-scan's worst-severity verdict drops from high to low/info relative to baseline, subject to: zero regression on hosts (rvm, pi-dev) that register no MCP server at all; full existing test suite stays green; new file covered by manifest provenance hashes.

baseline.scaffold: npx metaharness <name> --template minimal (pre-fix generator, captured via git stash)

regression_check_rvm.note: Unchanged pre/post fix -- confirms the gating condition (not an unconditional write) avoids a false mcpEnabled flip.

self_caught_defect.text: First draft of the fix wrote .harness/mcp-policy.json unconditionally for every scaffold. Self-testing against the rvm host (which never registers an MCP server) found this flipped mcpEnabled false->true and manufactured a new medium finding where none existed pre-fix. Rejected that draft; corrected to gate on the real rendered .claude/settings.json mcpServers / .mcp.json signal before any independent critic ran.

test_suite.result: 627/629 passed (2 pre-existing skips), 0 regressions, +4 new tests vs. pre-session baseline of 623/625

darwin.reason: Deterministic generator fix (emit-or-don't-emit a fixed JSON object on a boolean signal) has no tunable parameter space for bounded evolution to search. Consistent with prior security-adversarial nights (08-13,08-18,08-28,09-03,09-08,09-18), none of which ran Darwin.

reward_hack_check.text: Policy field names/values (defaultDeny, allowNetwork, allowShell, allowFileWrite, requireApprovalForDangerous, toolTimeoutMs, maxToolCallsPerTurn, auditLog) verified by direct source read to exactly match what mcp-scan.ts's policy checks (lines ~85-114) and ADR-022's specified default object expect -- not a shape that merely satisfies the scanner's keys without matching its semantics. No test weakened, no gold data modified, no corpus involved (static scanner only, no LLM eval).

independent_critic.agent: fresh general-purpose agent, no prior session context
checked: Read full diff live (2 files, purely additive, 0 deletions)
Read ADR-022, host-config.ts (all 9 non-claude-code hosts), mcp-scan.ts/oia-manifest.ts/score.ts/threat-model.ts mcpEnabled logic, LEDGER.md 2026-09-08 entry

git log --all --oneline | grep -i mcp-policy|mcp.scan : no prior commit writes .harness/mcp-policy.json from scaffold() -- confirms novelty against merged history
caveats: codex/hermes/openclaw/copilot/opencode hosts still ship a live, ungoverned MCP server with no policy file and no scanner coverage (verified live: --host codex produces .codex/config.toml with a real mcp_servers entry, no policy). Pre-existing, not worsened by this fix, already named as a separate disclosed-not-fixed item in LEDGER.md's 09-08 addendum (candidates #4/#5 in issue #297). Should not be read as having closed ADR-022 generally.

Critic has no GitHub network access from its sandbox, so could not rule out an in-flight duplicate open PR by searching GitHub directly -- mitigated by this session's own git log --all check plus direct inspection of the 3 most recent security-adversarial dream branches (2026-10-03 #372 budget-watchdog kill-switch, 2026-10-08 #380 dependency CVEs, 2026-10-13 threat-model.ts verdict grid), none of which touch index.ts's scaffold() or write mcp-policy.json.

security_review.text: This IS the security-adversarial finding for tonight; no separate higher-privilege surface touched. The fix only adds a JSON data file read by existing static scanners -- it does not change any runtime enforcement path, grant any new capability, or touch secrets/credentials handling.
